mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off channel, lowering near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by ≥ 25 bps
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such events are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed prior quarter median in 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the 12-month moving average accompanied by a decline in wage growth (HOUST) signals a labor market softening that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month moving average AND HOUST < 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such labor softening events, or wage growth recovers before unemployment claims fail to trend lower.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above the prior quarter's average, coupled with a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts a demand-supply imbalance favoring equities and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth acceleration (ΔΔINDPRO > 2.5%) AND CPIAUCSL < 12-month moving average for the current quarter
regime_hint: expansionary supply shock without persistent inflation
failure_condition: Rank IC for this signal < 0.05 over any 12-month window, or 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline in the same regime.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with a sustained drop in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) indicates softening demand, which typically precedes S&P 500 drawdowns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such supply softening are not negative in >70% of cases, or inflation recovers before production declines.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent monetary easing reflected by FEDFUNDS below 2% for three consecutive months is associated with a persistent upward bias in S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 2-year window, 60-day forward returns in such periods are not statistically higher than a neutral baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a regime indicator) coincides with a sharp rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) and precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average + 30% in one month
failure_condition: In 10 such events, 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of cases, or job openings data (not proxyable here) shows no correlation with the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time acceleration in retail sales demand proxy (not directly observable; using HOUST as a proxy for consumer activity) above trend, combined with a decline in industrial production (GDPC1), predicts a short-term bearish S&P 500 20-day return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average + 10% in one month AND GDPC1 < 12-month moving average for the same month
regime_hint: transitory demand surge in a contractionary economy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such events are not negative in >80% of occurrences, or HOUST decelerates before GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of double-digit year-over-year inflation (CPIAUCSL > 12-month YoY + 12%) combined with a sharp drop in consumer confidence proxies (not directly observable; using UNRATE as a stand-in) predicts a regime shift to supply-side risk and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 12-month YoY + 12% for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 12-month moving average
failure_condition: In 10 such inflation spikes, 20-day forward returns are not negative in more than 40% of cases, or UNRATE recovers before inflation accelerates.
